references.text: The main account of Israel's sin with Baal-Peor, where the people worshiped the idol and the Lord sent a plague that killed 24,000 people
Moses refers back to the incident at Peor where the Israelites were tempted into idolatry
Joshua reminds the people of the sin at Peor and its consequences as a warning
The psalmist describes how Israel attached themselves to Baal-Peor and ate sacrifices offered to dead gods, which led to the Lord's anger
Hosea mentions Baal-Peor as an example of Israel's early apostasy and shame
The continuation of the verse confirming that those who held fast to the Lord, unlike the worshipers of Baal-Peor, are still alive
Paul uses the incident at Baal-Peor as a warning against sexual immorality and idolatry for the Christians in Corinth
